label: Client discussion
title: Understand the goal.
description: I ask the client to walk me through a busy day. We pick one problem to solve and identify who needs the change.
clientTouchpoint: Ask clear questions, listen closely, and confirm the goal before moving forward.
outcome: A shared understanding of the problem.

label: Requirements
title: Define what matters.
description: With the team, I map who can do what. We turn a user journey into acceptance criteria the client can review.
clientTouchpoint: Review the requirements together and close gaps before development starts.
outcome: A brief everyone can build against.

label: Proposal
title: Present a practical plan.
description: I show the client what we can deliver first, which decisions can wait, and how those choices affect the timeline.
clientTouchpoint: Align on priorities, timing, and how changes should be handled.

label: Architecture
title: Design the foundation.
description: I trace one user action from the screen through the API to the database. That helps the team agree on responsibilities and access rules.
clientTouchpoint: Discuss the decisions that affect maintainability, cost, timeline, and future growth.

label: Build & test
title: Build, review, test.
description: I build a small slice of the workflow, review it with the team, and test what happens when something goes wrong.
clientTouchpoint: Share progress, demonstrate working features, and flag blockers early.

label: Delivery & deploy
title: Launch with confidence.
description: We check the release together. I walk the client through the live workflow and document what the team needs for handover.
clientTouchpoint: Walk through the release, confirm scope, and explain the important handover details.
outcome: A reviewed release and clear handover.

label: Ongoing support
title: Support what ships.
description: When a user reports an issue, I reproduce it, trace the cause, and check the fix against their original workflow.
clientTouchpoint: Keep communication open around new requests, issues, and support priorities.
outcome: Software that stays useful after release.
